# TftpdR 0.3.0

Feature release for the read-only TFTP (RFC 1350) server and native [Slint](https://slint.dev/) desktop panel. The panel now supports English and Simplified Chinese and offers follow-system, light and dark appearance modes. The daemon's level-based log filtering no longer pulls in the `regex` engine, reducing the GNU x64 daemon executable by about 21.6% compared with 0.2.2. The protocol, TOML configuration format, read-only behavior and server security defaults are unchanged.

**中文摘要**：0.3.0 是功能版本。GUI 新增英文/简体中文界面与跟随系统、浅色、深色外观；daemon 改用轻量级日志过滤，GNU x64 体积较 0.2.2 减少约 21.6%。TFTP 协议、TOML 配置格式、只读行为及服务端安全默认值不变。

## What's new

### English and Simplified Chinese UI

- The startup language follows the system locale: Simplified Chinese locales use Chinese; all others, including Traditional Chinese, use English.
- Static Slint text and Rust-generated messages (activity log, validation feedback and native dialog titles) use the same language.
- There is no runtime language switch; restart the panel after changing the system locale.

### Follow-system, light and dark appearance

- Appearance can follow the operating system or be set to Light or Dark in Settings.
- System theme changes are checked in the background while Follow system is selected.
- The preference is stored as local GUI state and does not change server configuration or restart the TFTP server.

### Smaller daemon log filtering

- Replaces `tracing-subscriber`'s `env-filter` with level/target filtering, removing the `regex` engine from the daemon dependency graph.
- GNU x64 `tftpd-r.exe`: 1,357,824 → 1,063,936 bytes (−293,888 bytes, −21.6%). GNU x64 GUI remains 9,036,288 bytes. Other targets must be measured independently.
- Supported directives: `off`/`error`/`warn`/`info`/`debug`/`trace` or `0`–`5`, `target=level`, and bare `target` (equivalent to `target=trace`), separated by commas. Span/field directives are not supported; invalid directives warn and are ignored.
- A target-only filter keeps the `info` default for other targets. For example, `--log tftpd_r_core=debug` enables core debug records while retaining daemon INFO messages.

### Existing 0.2.2 GUI workflow

This release also includes the GUI workflow shipped in 0.2.2: remembered root directory and recent-root menu, bounded local-time activity log with exact-level display filtering and explicit export, pre-warmed native folder picker, and unified titlebar/toolbar.

## Compatibility and security

- No breaking changes to the TFTP protocol, TOML schema, daemon/core defaults, read-only behavior or server security policy.
- Existing 0.2.x configuration files can be reused. Uploads remain disabled; the server remains read-only.
- GUI language and theme preferences are local UI state and do not affect daemon configuration.
- GNU x64 size measurements are informational and do not predict MSVC or arm64 sizes.

## Verification status

- Local Windows 11 / Rust 1.100.0 / GNU x64: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --offline` (211 passed, 1 ignored), and `cargo build --workspace --release --locked --offline` passed. The ignored test requires a desktop dialog session.
- GNU x64 release sizes: daemon 1,063,936 bytes; GUI 9,036,288 bytes.
- The release workflow runs fmt/clippy/tests on Windows MSVC and Linux GNU, then builds Windows/Linux × x64/arm64 on native runners. The 0.3.0 workflow/tag and final target artifacts have not yet been run or published.
- Not verified by this local run: interactive Linux GUI, arm64 runtime behavior, real/legacy TFTP client interoperability, LAN/firewall/TID behavior, privileged-port deployment, RDP, IME, accessibility, other DPIs, and system-theme changes on target desktops. See `docs/testing.md` for the detailed verification matrix.

Linux binaries use the runner's glibc; build from source on older distributions if necessary. The GUI requires an X11/Wayland desktop session; the daemon does not.

## Checksums

`SHA256SUMS` will be attached to the release; verify with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` or `Get-FileHash` on Windows.
